work.edition: Machine translation (gpt-6.1-sol, Patristica, 2026-10-26) of: Thoma Darmo (ed.), Thrissur: Mar Narsai Press, 1960; transcription on hudra.day (Hendo Academy), used with permission. Partial: 18/126 pages transcribed.

paragraphs.text:
†
By the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, we begin to print the Book of Before and After, the Cycle, the Collection, and the Treasury, and the Melody of Helps, together with the Book of Psalms, according to the order of Mar Gabriel and Mar Abraham of the Upper Monastery. Printing was completed at the press of Mar Narsai the Teacher, in the city of Thrissur in southern India, in the year of our Lord 1960.
1960.

The Book of Before and After.
The order of evening prayer for ordinary days, for the week of the first choir.
Instructions. First the superior, the bishop, begins. If he is not present, the archdeacon begins. If he is not there, the priest who is senior in ordination among the priests in his choir begins. Know also: if the day's prayer belongs to the first choir, it is to begin in the first choir. If it belongs to the second choir, it begins in the second. This is determined from the Cycle, except during the Fast. If the melody for the Sunday vigil is “The Lord reigns,” it belongs to the first choir; if it is “Then Moses sang praise,” it belongs to the second choir. Thus, if Sunday belongs to the first choir, Monday, Wednesday, and Friday also belong to the first choir. Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday are to belong to the second choir. The same applies to feasts and commemorations that fall on those days. The reverse applies if Sunday belongs to the second choir.
“Glory to God in the highest.” Repeat three times. “And on earth peace and good hope for humanity, at all times and forever. Amen.” They say, “Bless, my lord.” Then they continue in chant: “Our Father in heaven,

may your name be held holy; may your kingdom come. Holy, holy, holy are you. Our Father in heaven, heaven and earth are full of the [?] of your glory. Watchers and human beings cry out to you: Holy, holy, holy are you.” “Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy; may your kingdom come. May your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today the bread we need, and forgive us our debts, as we too have forgiven our debtors. Do not bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one. For yours are the kingdom, the power, and the glory, forever and ever. Amen.” The superior continues: “Glory to the Father, to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.” They respond: “From eternity and forever. Amen and amen.” “Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy; may your kingdom come. Holy, holy, holy are you. Our Father in heaven, heaven and earth are full of the greatness of your glory. Watchers and human beings cry out to you: Holy, holy, holy are you.” The deacon says: “Let us pray. Peace be with us.”
Prayer.
“Let us give thanks, my Lord, to your divinity and worship your lordship. Let us offer constant, unceasing glory to your glorious Trinity at all times, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.” They respond: “Amen.”
For Monday evening prayer of the first choir. Psalm sections. In the Lord I have placed my hope. How can you say to my soul? Lord, who may dwell in your tent? See page 249. Then the priest says the prayer of incense. Let us offer praise to your glorious Trinity at all times, forever. Amen. Or this prayer: Christ, who accepted the blood of the martyrs on the day they were killed, accept this incense from my feeble hands, through the grace of your compassion, forever. Amen. (He makes the sign of the cross over the censer and puts incense in it.)

He says the prayer “To you, Lord.” And for all your help and kindness toward us, which cannot be repaid, we will thank you and praise you without ceasing in your crowned Church, filled with every kind of help and every blessing, for you are the Lord and Creator of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever. They respond: Amen. Then both choirs say together: To you, Lord of all, we give thanks, and you, Jesus Christ, we praise, for you raise our bodies to life, and you are the Savior of our souls. (The refrain in church.) I rejoiced when they said to me, “We are going to the house of the Lord.” (Outside the church they say:) You are everywhere, God; accept our supplication. To you, Lord of all, we give thanks, and you, Jesus Christ, we praise, for you raise our bodies to life, and you are the Savior of our souls. Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, from eternity and forever. Amen and amen. To you, Lord of all, we give thanks, and you, Jesus Christ, we praise, for you raise our bodies to life, and you are the Savior of our souls. The deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us. Prayer of the first introductory chant. You, my Lord, truly raise our bodies to life, and you are the good Savior of our souls, and the constant guardian of our lives. To you, my Lord, we owe thanks, worship, and praise at all times, Lord of all… They [?]: Amen. They say the introductory chant in the first choir. First introductory chant. Save us, Lord, for the good person is no more. Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah. Save us, Lord, for the good person is no more. (a) Faithfulness has vanished from the earth. People speak empty words, each to his neighbor, with deceitful lips. They speak with a double heart. May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips and tongues that speak boastfully, those who say, “We will make our tongue powerful, and the lips—”
(a) This is how all the introductory chants begin.

“—are our own. Who is our master?” Because of the plundering of the poor and the groaning of the afflicted. “Now I will arise,” says the Lord, “and openly bring about salvation.” Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and amen. The members of the choir whose leader begins respond: “Hallelujah, hallelujah.” The members of the other choir respond: “Hallelujah.” The leader of the first choir begins the antiphons as follows: “Save us, Lord, for the good have vanished.” The whole choir joins in with him in unison. “Look, the good have vanished and come to an end.” Likewise, the other choir sings the antiphon that follows it. And so on... They proceed in this way through all the opening chants and all the antiphons, both the earlier and the later ones, on all the days of the ordinary weeks. The earlier antiphons. To the tune of “Look, he has taken me captive.”
Save us, Lord, for the good have vanished. Look, the good have vanished, the righteous have come to an end, and the faithful have perished. There is no one upright among human beings. Everyone speaks with a double heart, and each person speaks to his neighbor with deceitful lips. Our inner being is full of envy, deceit, and slander. Love, which is the foremost of the commandments, has been uprooted from our minds. Because of this, there is great fear that you may destroy us in your anger. Your justice has fallen silent toward us and has made room for your grace. Our Lord, have pity on us. The Lord is faithful in his words.
Our Savior promised the gift of life to those who cherish his love, and enriched them with knowledge of him. He filled them with the wisdom of his power and taught them to pray at all times: Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy. May your kingdom come to us. May your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us the bread we need, and do not lead us into temptation. But deliver us from the evil one, for yours are the kingdom, the power, and the glory. Glory... Mary, who bore the medicine of life for the children of Adam, may we find refuge through your supplication. Trusting in the prayers of Saint John, may we overcome the evil one and his power. And through the prayers of the prophets, apostles, martyrs, fathers, and teachers,

and through the prayers of our holy father, the confessors, and Saint George, and through the great power of the cross and the sanctification of the holy Church, let us implore Christ to show mercy and compassion to our souls. The deacon says: “Let us pray. Peace be with us.”
The prayer of “Lord, I have called upon you,” in the latter choir. To your mercy, our Lord and our God, and to the care of your will for us, we owe thanksgiving, worship, and praise at all times, Lord of all... And they [?]: “Amen.” And they say: Lord, I have called to you; answer me. Listen to my words and receive my prayer. Lord, I have called to you; answer me. Listen to my words and receive my prayer like incense before you. The offering of my hands is like the evening offering. Lord, set a guard over my mouth and a guard over my lips. Do not let my heart turn toward an evil word or let me commit deeds of injustice with wicked men. Let me not share a meal with them. Let a righteous person teach me and rebuke me. Let the oil of the wicked not anoint my head, for my prayer is against their wickedness. Their judges were restrained by the hand of the rock, and he heard my words, which are pleasant. Like a plowshare that splits the earth, their bones were scattered at the mouth of Sheol. But I have lifted my eyes to you, Lord, and I have trusted in you. Do not cast away my life. Protect me from the hands of the arrogant, who have hidden snares for me. Let the evildoers fall together into their own traps until I have passed by. With my voice I called to the Lord; with my voice I pleaded with the Lord. I laid my plea before him. I showed him my distress. When my spirit was troubled, you knew my paths. On the road where I walked, they hid snares for me. I looked to the right and saw that there was no one who acknowledged me. I had no place of refuge left, and no one cared for my life. I cried out to you, Lord, and said: You are my hope and my portion in the land of the living. Listen to my plea, because I have been brought low

so greatly. Rescue me from my persecutors, because they are stronger than I am. Bring my soul out of prison, so that I may give thanks to your name. Your righteous people will wait for me when you reward me. Your word is a lamp for my feet and a light for my paths. I have sworn and confirmed that I will keep your righteous judgments. I have been brought very low; Lord, give me life according to your word. Be pleased with the words of my mouth, Lord, and teach me your judgments. My life is always in your hands, and I have not forgotten your law. Sinners have set snares for me, but I have not strayed from your commandments. I have inherited your testimony forever, because it is the delight of my heart. I have turned my heart to carry out your commandments faithfully forever. Praise the Lord, all you peoples. Praise him, all nations, for his grace toward us has been mighty. Truly, the Lord is forever. Glory… Forever… And both choirs finish together. Lord, I have called to you; answer me. Listen to my words and receive my prayer. And the deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us. Prayer for the latter opening chant, in the second choir. Hear, our Lord and our God, the prayer of your servants in your compassion. And accept the petition of your worshipers in your mercy. Have compassion on our sinfulness through your grace and your mercies, healer of our bodies and good hope of our souls, Lord of all... And they respond: Amen. And they say the latter opening chant in the second choir.
The latter opening chant. Lord, who may dwell in your tent? Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah. And who may live on your holy mountain? The one who walks without blemish and does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart, and is not deceitful with his tongue, and does no evil to his companion, and accepts no bribe against his neighbor. The one who provokes anger is despised in his eyes, but he honors those who fear the Lord. Glory... Forever... And the members of the choir of the one who begins respond: Hallelujah, hallelujah. And they repeat—

the members of the other choir—Hallelujah. And they begin the latter responses like the earlier ones. The latter responses. To the tune of “He who knows thoughts.”
He who exists from before the ages. Compassionate Father, merciful Son, and brooding Spirit, sanctifier of the unclean, sanctify our bodies and our souls, and have mercy on us. Holy and awesome is his name. May the songs of holiness and the praises of the heavenly assemblies, together with the petition of the Son at the Father's right hand, appeal to your justice on our behalf; and have mercy on us. Glory... O Mary, mother of the King, the King of kings, plead with Christ, who shone forth from your womb, that he may have pity on us in his grace and make us worthy of his kingdom. Forever... Through the prayers of your saints, Christ our Savior—the prophets, apostles, martyrs, and all the righteous— protect the assembly of your worshipers from every harm. Let us say... Our holy father, be our guide in upright conduct that pleases your Lord, so that through your prayers we may be helped and may share in delight with you. (The deacon puts on the stole, fastens the belt, and stands in an orderly manner before the sanctuary.) And he says the litany in the first choir: Father of mercies. (See page 411.) And when it is finished, he adds: Let us entrust ourselves and one another to the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. And they respond: To you, Lord our God.
And the priest prays in the first choir: To you, Lord, mighty God, we entrust our bodies and our souls. And from you, our Lord and our God, we ask forgiveness of debts and sins. Grant us this in your grace and mercy, as you always do, Lord of all. The deacon who proclaimed the litany says: Raise your voices, all you people, and praise the living God. They say in a simple tone: Holy God, holy mighty one, holy immortal one, have mercy on us. Glory… Holy God, holy mighty one, holy immortal one,

have mercy on us. Forever… Holy God, holy mighty one, holy immortal one, have mercy on us. The deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
Prayer after “Holy God.” Holy, glorious, mighty, and immortal one, who dwells among the holy ones and finds delight in them: We implore you: turn toward us, my Lord, spare us, and have mercy on us, as you always do, Lord of all. They respond: Amen.
The deacon who made the proclamation says: Bless, my lord. Bow your heads for the laying on of hands and receive the blessing. The presiding priest says: May Christ make your ministry shine in the kingdom of heaven. He continues with the prayer. And as our souls agree in the one perfect faith in your glorious Trinity, may we all, in one harmony of love, be worthy to offer you praise, honor, thanksgiving, and worship at all times, Lord of all. They respond: Amen.
They say the evening response as prescribed in the Kashkul; it is the same as the response for the mysteries of the day. Glory… A supplementary hymn suited to the melody, or this one, to “Blessed Martyrs.”
It is said at the beginning of every week. The first choir begins.
I earnestly hoped in the Lord. The poor shall eat and be satisfied. The body of Christ and his precious blood are on the holy altar. Let us all approach him with reverence and love. And with the angels let us acclaim him: Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God. Repeat. Glory… Christ, refuge and sure hope of those in distress, be a wall for your worshipers, my Lord, and guard them from the evil one. Heal and bind up their wounds through the compassion of your divinity, merciful one who forgives sins. The deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
Prayer of the Alphabet, in the second choir. Spare us in your grace, compassionate one, and turn toward us, you who are full of mercy. My Lord, do not withhold

your attention and care from us, for our hope and trust are in you at every time and season, Lord of all… They respond: Amen.
The Alphabet. Blessed are those whose way is blameless, Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah. And who walk in the law of the Lord. Blessed are those who keep his testimony and seek him with their whole heart. They have done no wrong, but have walked in his ways. You commanded that your commandments be kept with great diligence. If only my ways were made firm so that I might keep your commandments! Then I would not be ashamed when I kept all your commandments. I will thank you with an upright heart when I have learned your righteous judgments. I have kept your commandments; do not abandon me forever. How can a young man keep his way pure? By keeping your commandments. With all my heart I have sought you; do not let me stray from your commandments. I have hidden your words in my heart so that I may not sin against you. Blessed are you, Lord; teach me your commandments. With my lips I have recounted all your righteous judgments. I have loved the way of your testimony far more than all wealth. I have pondered your commandments and have come to know your ways. I have pondered your law so that I may not forget your words. Glory… Forever… And they respond: Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah. Then they continue with “Our Father in heaven,” with its refrain, as at the beginning. When it is finished, the deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
Prayer. May your holy name, our Lord and our God, be praised; may your divinity be worshiped, and your lordship honored; may your greatness be glorified and your being exalted; and over your people and the sheep of your pasture may the everlasting mercies of your glorious Trinity flow at all times, Lord of all… And they respond: Amen. Bless, my lord. Its conclusion. In heaven and on earth, blessed, my Lord, is your divinity, and worshiped is your lordship. Holy and glorious and praised, high and exalted is the worshiped and praised name of your glorious Trinity, at all times, Lord

of all… And they respond: Amen. Then they continue with the hymn of the martyrs appointed for the evening of the day: Holy martyrs, pray. See page 420.
Prayer after the evening hymn of the martyrs.
Prayer. To you, who exalt your church, crown those who love you, and grant victory to your athletes, and help your saints in their glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine contests, we plead: Turn toward us, my Lord, and have pity and mercy on us, as you always do, Lord of all. And they respond: Amen. Bless, my lord.
Another prayer. Through the prayer of your saints, our Lord and our God, be reconciled to us; and through the supplication of your faithful ones, remove our sins, forgive our shortcomings, make our enemies peaceful, and raise our departed ones to life; and make us worthy of the splendid glory of your kingdom, together with the upright and righteous who fulfill your will in Jerusalem above, Lord of all. And they respond: Amen. Bless, my lord.
Then they continue with the Prayer for Help, which is said only in church.
Prayer. May the help of your mercies, my Lord, and the great assistance of your grace, and the hidden and glorious power of your glorious Trinity, And with your right hand, full of mercy and compassion, shelter and sustain the weakness of your worshipers. From your holy house, full of every help and every good thing, through the prayers of all your saints who please you, Lord of all… They respond [?]: Amen. Bless, my lord.
They continue: With your blessing, our Lord and our God, may your servants be blessed. And through the care of your will may your worshipers be protected. And may the enduring peace of your divinity, my Lord, and the lasting peace of your lordship reign among your people and in your church, all the days of the world, Lord of all… They respond: Amen. Bless, my lord.
(And if there are many priests, let each one of them say one of the following prayers, according to the seniority of his ordination.

After each prayer that is said, they respond: Amen. Bless, my lord.)
Another prayer. May the blessing of the one who blesses all, the peace of the one who gives peace to all, the compassion of the one who has compassion on all, and the protection of our worshipful God be with us, among us, and around us, and protect us from the evil one and his forces, at all times and seasons, Lord of all…
Another prayer. With your blessing, our Lord and our God, may we be blessed, and through your care may we be protected. May your power come to our aid, may your help accompany us, and may your right hand shelter us. May your peace reign among us, and may your cross be a high wall and a place of refuge for us. Beneath its wings may we find shelter from the evil one and his forces, at all times and [?], Lord of all… Another prayer. Blessed, my Lord, are the mercies of your grace, and worthy of worship are the promises of your lordship, which always teach us to look to you and glory in you, and not to give up our hope in you, all the days of our lives, Lord of all… Another prayer. May your blessing, our Lord and our God, rest upon your people, and may your compassion always be upon us, weak and sinful as we are, our good hope, our refuge full of mercy, and the one who forgives debts and sins, Lord of all…
Another prayer. May the peace of the Father be with us, and the love of the Son among us, and may the Holy Spirit guide us according to his will. And may his mercy and compassion be upon us, at all [?] and seasons, Lord of all…
Another prayer. May your peace, my Lord, dwell in us, may your harmony rule within us, and may your love increase among us, all the days of our lives, Lord of all…
Another prayer. With your right hand, my Lord, protect us, and beneath your wings shelter us, and may your help accompany us, all the days of our lives, Lord of all…
Another prayer. Give us, my Lord, enduring peace, love, and a love of learning, and life, good things, and joys, and food that will not fail us, all the days of our lives, Lord of all…

Another. Be a guardian who never sleeps over the fold where your sheep dwell: so that it may not be harmed by wolves thirsty for the blood of your flock; for you are an inexhaustible sea, Lord of all... Another. Bless us with your blessings, our Lord, and surround us with the wall of your care: Do not let us lack good things, and seat us at the feast in the bridal chamber of your light, Lord of all...
Another. Come to our aid, my Lord, in your compassion, and reveal yourself for our salvation in your mercy: and direct our steps along the paths of righteousness all the days of our lives, Lord of all... Another. Let your grace shine upon us, my Lord, when your justice judges us: and let your mercy come to our aid on the day when your majesty shines forth, Lord of all...
Another. May your blessing and your grace and your right hand, full of mercy and compassion, overshadow and accompany the assembly of your worshipers: who call upon you and plead with you at all times and seasons, Lord of all...
Another. Bless, my Lord, by your grace, and protect in your mercy the assembly of believers: who trust in you and call upon your holy name and plead with you at all times, Lord of all.
Another. Be with us always in your mercy, my Lord, and guide us according to the will of your divinity all the days of our lives, Lord of all... Another. May a blessing of mercy, my Lord, from the treasury of mercy, through the angel of mercy: be sent from God, who abounds in mercy, and be poured out upon the assemblies of those who praise you: who constantly call upon your holy name and look and wait for mercy and for the salvation that comes from you, Lord of all... And they continue: May the prayer, my Lord, of the holy Virgin, the petition of the blessed Mother, and the supplication and entreaty of her who is full of grace:

my Lady, blessed Mary; and the great power of the victorious cross, and divine help, and the petition of Saint John the Baptist: and of the blessed apostles, and of the illustrious fathers, heralds of righteousness and sowers of peace throughout creation; and of our pure and holy father, Saint Aba the Catholicos, and Saint Stephen, the first of the martyrs: and of the mighty warrior Saint George, the illustrious martyr, and of Saint So-and-so... and of blessed Saint Eugene and his entire spiritual company; and of Shmuni and her sons, and of all the martyrs and saints of our Lord: be for us always a high wall and a strong refuge: to redeem, deliver, rescue, and protect our bodies and souls from the evil one and his forces at all times and seasons, Lord of all... And they [?]: Amen.
Then they conclude with the choir that follows. The priest takes the cross in his right hand. He stands on the south side, turns his face toward the people, and says: Bless, my lord. With your permission. They answer: By the command of Christ our Lord, and glory to his holy name. The people bow their heads. He then adds the concluding prayer: Glory to you, Jesus, our victorious King, radiance of the eternal Father, begotten without beginning, above times and created things. We have no hope or expectation except you, the Creator. Through the prayers of the righteous and the chosen, who have pleased you from the beginning, grant atonement for our sins and forgiveness for our offenses, deliverance from our troubles and answers to our petitions. Bring us to your glorious light, and guard us by your living standard from every harm, hidden and visible, (Christ, the hope of our nature), now ♱ and at all times and forever and ever. He makes the sign of the cross over the people, extending his hand upward toward the west and bringing it toward the east. Then he extends it toward the south side and moves it toward the north side, so that the sacred object comes to rest on the north side, which is the

left side of the congregation. They answer: May Christ hear your prayers. May Christ make your priesthood shine in the kingdom of heaven. Another. May the prayer of your weak servants be accepted, our Lord and our God, before the judgment seat of your divinity. May this gathering of ours satisfy the will of your lordship, so that through grace we may receive from you health of body, protection of the soul, and an abundant supply of food, (atonement for offenses and forgiveness of sins), and, my Lord, constant tranquility, lasting peace, and loving harmony that neither passes away nor dissolves among us throughout the whole time that this world endures, (Christ, the hope of our nature), now… ♱
Another. Blessed is God forever, and praised is his holy name from generation to generation. We petition him and implore the overflowing sea of his mercy, that he may make us worthy of the splendid glory of his kingdom, of delight with his holy angels, and of confidence before him, and of standing at his right hand in the Jerusalem above, through his grace and his mercies, (Christ, the hope of our nature), now… ♱
Another. God, Lord of all, in whose house we have gathered and before whose majesty we have prayed, in the great hope of his mercy—may he hear our prayer in his kindness and accept our petition in his compassion. May he wash and cleanse the filth of our offenses and sins with the abundant hyssop of his compassion. May he give rest to the souls of our departed in the glorious dwellings of his kingdom, and sprinkle upon us all the dew of his kindness. And may the right hand of his providence shield us and all creatures, through his grace and mercy: (Christ, the hope of our nature) now… ♱
Another. God, Lord of all, who has placed his praises in our mouths and his songs on our tongues, and his melodies in our throats, and thanksgiving to him on our lips, and faith in him in our hearts—may he hear our prayers and accept our petitions, and be gracious toward our supplications, (and forgive our sins,) and grant us our requests

that are good and blameless. And from the great treasury of his compassion may he pour out his mercy and kindness upon us and upon the whole world in its entirety: (Christ, the [?] of our nature) now… ♱
Another. May the name of God, Lord of all, be praised among us, who orders the times and seasons. And over us, weak and sinful, and over the whole world in its entirety, and over the holy Church and her children, and over our fathers, our masters, our teachers, and our departed, and the departed who have left and passed away from among us, and over our entire brotherhood in Christ, may the right hand of his providence and compassion spread its protection: (Christ, the hope of our nature) now… ♱
Another. Glory to God, honor to the angels, shame to Satan, and worship to the cross; exaltation to the Church, resurrection to the departed, acceptance to the repentant, and release to prisoners; health and healing to the sick and infirm, and great tranquility and peace to the four corners of the world. And upon us also, who are weak and sinful, may the kindness and mercy of our worshipful God come, spread their protection, overflow, remain, and reign continually: (Christ, the hope of our nature) now… ♱
Another. (By the right hand of your lordship, our Father in heaven): bless us all, Lord, and protect us all, and help us all, and support and shelter us all, and raise the departed of us all, and extend your right hand in protection over us all. And may your mercy and kindness be poured out upon us all; and may praise, honor, thanksgiving, worship, and continual gratitude ascend to you from the mouths of us all: (Christ, the [?] of our nature) now… ♱
Another. May God, Lord of all, bless our gathering by his grace, and protect our congregation through the overflowing abundance of his compassion, and grant our requests from his treasury. And upon the whole world in its entirety, and upon

the holy Church and her children, and upon this country and its inhabitants, and upon this monastery and its residents, and upon all of us together, may the kindness and mercy of our good God come and be poured out continually: (Christ, the hope of our nature) now… ♱
And they follow this with the creed of the three hundred and eighteen fathers, the bishops who assembled at Nicaea, a city of Bithynia, in the time of the victorious Emperor Constantine. The reason for their assembly was the wickedness of Arius. According to the custom that prevails among the members of our holy and apostolic Church of the East, and that has long been observed, from ancient days: Through the tradition and transmission of the ancients, who were versed in contemplations of divine truth, it has continued down to our own days. And so we begin to recite the Nicene rule of faith. For truly, without doubt: We believe in one God, the Father almighty, maker of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, the firstborn of all creation, who was begotten of his Father before all ages and was not made; true God from true God, of the same nature as his Father; through whose hands the worlds were established and everything was created; who for us human beings and for our salvation came down from heaven, and took flesh from the Holy Spirit and became human, and was conceived and born of the Virgin Mary. He suffered and was crucified in the days of Pontius Pilate, and was buried, and rose after three days, as it is written. He ascended into heaven and sat at the right hand of his Father, and he is to come again to judge the dead and the living. And in one Holy Spirit, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, the life-giving Spirit. And in one holy, apostolic, catholic Church.

And we acknowledge one baptism for the forgiveness of sins, and the resurrection of our bodies, and life for ever and ever. Amen.
…
For Tuesday evening, of the First.
Psalm sections. To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul. To you, Lord, I have called; my God, do not be silent toward me. See page 261. (For the notice concerning the prayers, opening chants, and responses, see Monday of the First, page 1.)
First opening chant. Hear, holy Lord, and look upon my petition. Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah. And listen to the prayer [?], which does not come from deceitful lips. Let my judgment come forth from your presence. Let your eyes see what is right. You have examined my heart and visited me at night. You have tested me and found no wrongdoing in me. Nor have the deeds of human beings passed over my mouth, in the speech of lips. Rather, you have kept me from my evil ways. You have upheld my movements in your paths, so that my steps may not falter. I have called upon you because you have answered me. Glory. Forever.
First responses. To “Light and Son of Light.”
Hear, O God, and have mercy on me. He hears and does not neglect; he answers, delivers, and saves. Hear our plea, my Lord, and in your mercy answer our requests. The Lord is faithful in his words. Our Lord, you said: “For everyone who knocks at the door of my lordship, the door is opened, and their requests are answered.” Glory... May the prayer of the Virgin Mary, the mother of Christ, be a wall for us and protect us from the evil one. Forever... Prophets and apostles, martyrs, priests, and teachers, may your prayer be a wall for us.
